record.context_brief: Threshold-graph covering and density extremal questions.
record.original_question: Using threshold graphs instead of cliques, determine the correct extremal behavior of threshold-graph coverings and large threshold subgraphs. In particular: (i) if a graph family has nth member edge-coverable by 2n threshold graphs but requiring 3n threshold graphs for an edge-partition, is that 3n requirement best possible? and (ii) if a graph with 2n vertices and n^2 + 1 edges must contain a threshold subgraph with n(1 + 1/2) edges, what is the correct constant c for which one can force a threshold subgraph with cn edges?

evidence.quote: I have a family of graphs such that the nth graph can be edge-covered by 2n threshold graphs, but requires 3n threshold graphs to edge-partition it. Is this best possible?
We think it need not contain a threshold graph with n(1 + 5/8) edges. What is the correct multiple of n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A threshold graph is a graph that can be constructed from a single vertex by repeatedly adding either an isolated vertex or a dominating vertex (one adjacent to all existing vertices). Equivalently, threshold graphs are exactly the graphs containing no induced subgraph isomorphic to 2K_2, P_4, or C_4.

Consider the following two extremal questions about threshold graphs.

(i) Cover vs. partition. Suppose there exists a family of graphs {G_n} such that, for every n, the edge set E(G_n) can be covered by the edge sets of 2n threshold subgraphs of G_n (these threshold subgraphs may overlap), but any partition of E(G_n) into edge-disjoint threshold subgraphs requires at least 3n parts. Determine whether the ratio 3n/2n = 3/2 is the largest possible separation. More precisely, find the supremum of constants c such that there exists a graph family in which the minimum size of a threshold edge-cover is m_n while the minimum size of a threshold edge-partition is at least c·m_n + o(m_n).

(ii) Large threshold subgraphs in dense graphs. Determine the largest constant c with the following property: every graph on 2n vertices with at least n^2 + 1 edges contains a threshold subgraph with at least cn edges. Equivalently, find
   c* = lim inf_{n→∞} (1/n) · min { t(G) : |V(G)| = 2n, |E(G)| ≥ n^2 + 1 },
where t(G) denotes the maximum number of edges in a threshold subgraph of G.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of either the cover-versus-partition ratio question or the precise extremal constant for forcing a large threshold subgraph in graphs on 2n vertices with more than n^2 edges. General references on extremal graph theory and edge partitions appear, but none specifically settle these threshold-graph problems, so the current status is inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: Extremal Problems for Partitions of Edge Sets of Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Thesis on extremal partitioning problems for edge sets of graphs; does not address the specific threshold-graph cover/partition ratio.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the threshold-graph 2n vs 3n problem found.

status_evidence.title: Extremal Problems in Graph Saturation and Covering
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style document on saturation and covering problems; threshold-graph extremal subgraph constant not determined here.
status_evidence.claim: No determination of the constant c for forcing cn-edge threshold subgraphs.
